title: Caption Styles for Short Videos
metaDescription: Five caption styles for short videos, from bold word-by-word highlights to quiet TV-style subtitles. Each one is a starting point you can adjust.
intro: Supertitle comes with five caption styles, from loud word-by-word highlights to quiet subtitles on a bar. Pick the one that fits your video, then adjust it: the export looks exactly like the preview.

presets.bold: Big uppercase words in the middle of the frame, with a highlight box on the word being spoken. Made for fast, punchy vertical videos.
presets.word: The spoken word changes color as it's said, in a heavy sans-serif near the bottom of the frame.
presets.podcast: Longer lines with the upcoming words dimmed, so viewers can read along. Suits interviews and podcast clips.
presets.classic: Plain text on a dark bar, like TV subtitles. Calm and readable on any background.
presets.minimal: A serif face with a soft shadow and no highlight. Quiet captions for polished, considered videos.

faq.question: Can I change a style after picking it?
faq.answer: Yes. Each preset is a starting point: you can change the font, size, colors, highlight, position and more, and the preview updates as you go.

faq.question: Does the exported video look like the preview?
faq.answer: Yes. The editor and the export draw the captions with the same fonts and the same rules, so the MP4 matches what you saw.

faq.question: Which style works best with the sound off?
faq.answer: Styles that highlight the word being spoken, like Bold Highlight and Word Highlight, make it easy to follow along without audio. Classic is the calmest choice for longer talks.

faq.question: How many words show at once?
faq.answer: Each preset has its own default, from a few words in Bold Highlight to a full line in Classic. You can change the words per caption in the editor.
